text:
nidhi: we should standardize the gateway <-> edge admission handshake for backpressure. current behavior is ad-hoc per-pop and makes client sdk backoff inconsistent. idea: small status layer that returns structured hint headers for both unary and streaming.

aj: love it. what headers/payload are you thinking? keep it tiny so LB/proxies don't drop them.

nidhi: minimal: `X-Edge-Admission: allow|queue|reject` plus `X-Edge-Retry-Bucket: b1` and `Retry-After` (ms). For streaming, reply with initial frame `ADMIT:queue:wait=50` vs `ADMIT:allow` so client knows whether to open a streaming TX or not.

ken: SRE: prefer machine-readable JSON in a single header like `X-Edge-Admission: v=1;action=queue;wait_ms=50;bucket=b1` so we can extend later. but keep parse cheap.

sarah: telemetry question: we need per-admission-tag metrics: admit_action, wait_ms, downstream_outcome (success/rejected/retried). Also streaming partial-accept counts.

maria: tradeoff: early-queueing adds headroom but increases connection count. for long-poll streaming, queueing could mean holding a connection for ~wait_ms which is bad. Maybe queue only for <100ms. For longer waits, reply reject + hint.

nidhi: agreed. threshold rule: if streaming_request && wait_ms > 120 -> reject with `Retry-After` and `bucket`. Otherwise queue with close wait.

admit-bot: config-snapshot: admission.v1.rules = [{match: "*", action: "queue", max_wait_ms: 100}, {match: "x-client-priority=high", action: "allow"}]

aj: what about idempotency and side-effects? queued admission could accept presubmit and later fail, causing double side-effects if client retries. need a token. suggestion: `X-Admission-Token` returned when queued; client must present it when retrying to reconcile.

ken: implementation nit: store token in ephemeral in-pop kv with TTL ~2min. token->admit-record. If record later transitions to allow->forwarded we exchange token for execution. If client retries without token, treat as new request. risks: storage pressure if we get lots of queued requests.

maria: can we avoid server-side state by using signed tokens (HMAC) encoding admit-id and expiry? that reduces storage but risks replay if signed key leaks. tradeoff ok for short expiry.

aj: for streaming handshake, propose 2-phase: 1) preflight (HEAD-like) to ask for admission; 2) if allow, client opens stream with `X-Admission-Token`. We should hide this in SDK so product teams don't change UX.

sarah: metrics/alert: add `admission_backpressure_ratio` and `stream_preauth_fail_rate`. set burn-in threshold at 0.5% global and per-tenant 2% day1.

deploy-bot: canary deploy queued admission adapter to 10% POPs starting now :rocket:

nidhi: rollout plan: observe-only (emit headers but no queueing) -> preflight API + SDK plumbing -> per-tenant enable -> pop-canary -> global. will write RFC.

ken: one more: HTTP/2 and gRPC multiplexing caveat: holding half-closed streams uses connection resources. ensure gateway enforces per-connection stream cap when queueing to avoid head-of-line.

maria: and docs: show examples for unary and streaming SDKs and failure modes (what to do with admission tokens, how to backoff).

aj: ok. I'll own RFC draft. @sarah can you draft the dashboards? @ken will prototype token format.

sarah: on it.

nidhi: thanks all — leaving open for comments for 24h. :+1:
